instruction: Find the meaning and origin of the name Emma

metadata.explanation: Task variation that asks to find information about the name Emma. Uses pattern matching to verify the user navigated to Emma's name details page on babycenter.com. The pattern matches any URL starting with 'https://www.babycenter.com/baby-names/details/emma-' followed by any ID number.
metadata.verification_notes: Uses existing is_expected_url_pattern_match metric to check URL pattern. This is more robust than exact URL matching since we cannot verify the exact name ID without accessing the live website.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies navigation to Emma's name details page on babycenter.com using URL pattern matching
Getter (get_active_url_from_accessTree) can correctly extract the active tab's URL from the accessibility tree
Metric (is_expected_url_pattern_match) correctly performs regex pattern matching on the URL
Expected regex pattern is properly formatted and will match any babycenter.com URL for Emma's name details
Data flow is semantically correct: URL string extraction -> regex pattern matching

Minor coverage limitation: evaluator verifies navigation to the page but cannot verify that the user actually viewed/read the meaning and origin information (which is inherent to the instruction 'find the meaning and origin'). However, this is a practical limitation of web automation - verifying navigation to the details page is a reasonable proxy for task completion.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding additional verification to check if specific content (e.g., meaning/origin sections) is present on the page, though this may be fragile due to website changes
Current approach is pragmatic given that exact URL with ID cannot be known without accessing the live website, and pattern matching provides good coverage
